brief.task: Install uv 0.13.6 and follow the uv projects guide: create a new project called hello-world with `uv init`, then run the project's hello-world entrypoint with `uv run` so that it prints its greeting.

eligibility.notable_because: Backlog: uv is on the WATCHLIST backlog and not yet tested; the default Python package/project tool agents reach for

scout.why_notable: Backlog pick, and the one CLI in the slate. uv 0.13.6 shipped 2026-10-27 (19 wheels on PyPI); the installer pins by URL path, and the projects guide's layout (src/hello_world, `uv run hello-world`) differs from the older flat main.py template many agents remember.

launch_claims.claim: A specific version can be installed by including it in the installer URL: `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.13.6/install.sh | sh`.
launch_claims.testable_how: Run the versioned installer in a fresh box and compare `uv --version` to the version in the URL.

scout.found_via: WATCHLIST backlog; version from GitHub latest release and PyPI
scout.notes: The getting-started 'first steps' page only runs `uv` for its help text (not a useful check), so the task is the projects guide's first example, whose shown output is `Hello from hello-world!`. The check also cats any .venv/pyvenv.cfg under /work so a bare echo can't pass: uv writes `uv = <version>` there when `uv run` creates the env. Release notes say 2026-10-26; GitHub and PyPI timestamps say 2026-10-27 UTC.
